cards.text: Here's a song by David, king of Israel, set to the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.' He opens by calling out the rulers with two questions. 'Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?'

cards.question: David just asked the rulers if they speak justly and judge uprightly. What answer does he give?

answers.text: No they devise injustice in their hearts
Yes they judge the people fairly
He leaves the answer up to God

cards.text: Then David talks about the wicked and the liars. And he goes WAY back, to how far back their wandering goes.

cards.question: David says the wicked and the liars only start going astray once they grow up.

cards.text: Now David reaches for a picture. Their venom is like a snake's venom, like a cobra, but this cobra has one strange habit.

cards.question: In David's picture, what does the cobra do when the charmer plays his tune?
David compares the wicked to a cobra that won't hear the charmer's tune. What is he saying about them?

cards.text: Friend, I WAS that cobra in the back of the junk drawer: somebody says 'cheer up,' and my ears SLAM shut. Then the song turns, and David prays straight to God, asking Him to shatter their teeth in their mouths.

cards.question: Next David pictures lions, and he asks the LORD to tame them so they lie down in peace.

cards.text: David keeps praying: may they vanish like water that runs off. GONE. Like a tray of warm cookies in the Millers' kitchen.

cards.question: David asks that when the wicked draw the bow, their arrows will be blunted.

cards.text: Then come two more pictures, and they're heavy ones: a slug that dissolves in its slime, and a woman's stillborn child.

cards.question: Like a slug that dissolves and a stillborn child, David asks that the wicked never see the ___

cards.text: Next David pictures pots sitting over a fire of burning thorns. Friend, my oven takes so long to preheat, I stand there staring at it like it owes me money.

cards.question: Before the pots can even feel the burning thorns, green or dry, what happens to the wicked?
Now the song turns to the righteous. David says they will rejoice when they see they are avenged.

cards.text: Then comes a hard, vivid picture. David says the righteous 'will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.'

cards.question: When it's all over, people will say there is surely a ___ for the righteous
David started by asking if the rulers judge uprightly. At the end, people say there is surely someone who judges the earth. Who?

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences. 'Here's a song...' and 'He opens by calling out...' are followed by the two quoted questions from Psalm 58:1, which are two more sentences.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The setup says David is 'calling out the rulers.' That tells the baker his answer is an accusation, which rules out card 2's wrong answers 'Yes they judge the people fairly' and 'He leaves the answer up to God' before the question is asked.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Psalm 58:2 has two halves: the rulers devise injustice in their hearts, and with their hands they mete out violence on the earth. No card ever tells or asks about the violence half.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The setup says David 'goes WAY back' to show how far back their wandering goes. That gives away card 4's answer: the statement that they only go astray once they grow up is plainly False.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer moment: someone telling Papa Dorin 'cheer up' and his ears slamming shut. The backstory has no such moment. It says he went quiet and didn't talk much. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, but not new events in the drawer.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The blank is the last word of the line 'may they never see the sun.' Sun, moon and rain all fit the image, so nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out 'sun.' The baker is guessing wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: In Psalm 58:9 the core action is speed: He sweeps them away before the pots even feel the heat. The joke is about the oven taking a long time to preheat, which is waiting, the opposite action. That muddies the picture right before card 15 asks about it.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
